name: X-linked Spastic Paraplegia Type 34

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked Spastic Paraplegia Type 34

criteria.description: Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness
Positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance
Pathogenic mutation in the ATP13A2 gene confirmed by genetic testing
Absence of significant cognitive impairment or other neurological disorders
Normal or nonspecific brain MRI findings

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive lower limb spasticity with a positive family history of X-linked inheritance and identification of a pathogenic ATP13A2 gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation may overlap with other hereditary spastic paraplegias.

common.symptomName: Impaired vibration sensation in the lower limbs

imaging: Brain MRI usually normal or shows mild nonspecific white matter changes
Spinal cord MRI may show mild atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in ATP13A2 gene (X-linked inheritance)
other: Electromyography (EMG) and nerve conduction studies usually normal or show mild abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset with pure spastic paraplegia phenotype
Presence of cerebellar ataxia and optic neuropathy

redFlags: Rapid progression of spasticity and weakness
Presence of seizures or optic atrophy
references: Orphanet: X-linked spastic paraplegia type 34 - ORPHA:171607
Harding AE. Hereditary spastic paraplegias. Semin Neurol. 1993;13(4):333-342.
